title: Graphs of Tangent, Secant and Cosecant
short: Find asymptotes where cosine or sine is zero.
trouble: Students give tangent the same period as sine, 2π instead of π.

blocks.html: The other four trig functions are quotients, so their graphs have a feature sine and cosine never have: vertical asymptotes, where the denominator is zero.

$y = \tan x$ has period $\pi$, zeros at $x = k\pi$, vertical asymptotes at $x = \frac{\pi}{2} + k\pi$, and range all real numbers. $\sec x = \frac{1}{\cos x}$ has asymptotes where $\cos x = 0$; $\csc x$ and $\cot x$ have them where $\sin x = 0$. The period of $A\tan(Bx)$ is $\frac{\pi}{B}$; the period of $A\sec(Bx)$ is $\frac{2\pi}{B}$.

$\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$. As $x$ approaches $\frac{\pi}{2}$, $\cos x$ shrinks toward $0$ while $\sin x$ stays near $1$, so the quotient grows without bound: an asymptote. Tangent repeats every $\pi$ (not $2\pi$) because a half turn flips the signs of both sine and cosine, and their quotient stays the same. For secant, the reciprocal of a number between $-1$ and $1$ is at least $1$ in size, so $\sec x$ never lies strictly between $-1$ and $1$.

blocks.title: Asymptotes of secant
blocks.q: Find the vertical asymptotes of $y = \sec x$ on $[0, 2\pi)$.
steps: $\sec x = \frac{1}{\cos x}$ is undefined where $\cos x = 0$.

blocks.html: Giving tangent the period of sine, $2\pi$. Check two values: $\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1$ and $\tan\frac{5\pi}{4} = 1$ as well, only $\pi$ later. The graph repeats every $\pi$.

blocks.cap: Tangent is the height where the terminal side meets the line $x = 1$. Near $\frac{\pi}{2}$ the side is almost vertical and that height runs off the chart.
